rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A satellite orbits when gravity supplies the centripetal force: v₀ = √(GM/r) and T = 2π√(r³/GM). Energy is K = GMm/2r, U = −GMm/r, E = −GMm/2r. Orbital speed is mass-independent; higher orbits are slower but longer-period. Weightlessness arises from continuous free fall.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
g = GM/r²
v_orb = √(GM/r)
v_esc = √(2GM/r)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Orbital Velocity Derivation:** $v_0 = \sqrt{GM/r}$ comes from equating gravitational force to centripetal force: $GMm/r^2 = mv_0^2/r$. This applies to *circular* orbits around a spherically symmetric mass. The satellite's mass cancels out — all satellites at the same radius have the same speed.  ·  **Period Law:** $T = 2\pi\sqrt{r^3/GM}$ is Kepler's third law for circular orbits. Squaring gives $T^2 \propto r^3$, independent of satellite mass. This is valid only for bound circular/elliptical orbits — not for escape trajectories ($E \ge 0$).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: r is measured from the centre of Earth: r = R + h, never forget to add the radius.  ·  Orbital speed is ~7.9 km/s at the surface, 7.66 km/s at the ISS altitude, 3.08 km/s at geostationary.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Worked: identify given → pick sub-concept → apply standard form → check units / edges.  ·  LEO speed: v = √(gR) = √(9.8×6.4×10⁶) ≈ 7.9 km/s.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Orbital velocity v₀ = √(GM/r) follows from gravity = centripetal force.  ·  Period T = 2π√(r³/GM) — Kepler's third law.  ·  Orbital speed is independent of satellite mass.  ·  Energy: K = GMm/2r, U = −GMm/r, E = −GMm/2r.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: • Motion of a satellite: orbital velocity  ·  • Time period of the satellite  ·  v₀ = √(GM/r) — orbital speed depends only on radius, not satellite mass.  ·  T = 2π√(r³/GM) — Kepler's third law: T² ∝ r³.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Newton: F = G m₁m₂/r²; g = GM/r²; at Earth's surface g = GM/R² ≈ 9.8 m/s².  ·  Orbital velocity v = √(GM/r); time period T = 2π√(r³/GM); escape velocity v_esc = √(2GM/r) = √2·v_orbital (at same r).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: solve / apply for "Motion of a satellite: orbital velocity and time period o…" and verify the answer is plausible.  ·  A satellite orbits at 200 km above Earth. Find its orbital speed and period.  ·  Find the height at which a satellite has an orbital period of 2 hours.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Energy numericals (K, U, E) for a given orbit are frequently asked.  ·  Conceptual: 'why do astronauts float?' — answer free fall.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: ISS period ≈ 93 minutes at r = 6.8×10⁶ m.  ·  Geostationary altitude ≈ 35,800 km; v ≈ 3.08 km/s.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Fact.** Newton: F = G m₁m₂/r²; g = GM/r²; at Earth's surface g = GM/R² ≈ 9.8 m/s².  ·  **Fact.** Orbital velocity v = √(GM/r); time period T = 2π√(r³/GM); escape velocity v_esc = √(2GM/r) = √2·v_orbital (at same r).  ·  **Fact.** For a uniform sphere, g ∝ r inside and g = 0 at the centre; g decreases as 1/r² outside.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Weightlessness = free fall.  ·  T² ∝ r³ (Kepler)  ·  Orbital velocity: v₀ = √(GM/r)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Near-surface orbital speed: v₀ = √(gR)  ·  Time period: T = 2πr/v₀ = 2π√(r³/GM)  ·  Kinetic energy: K = GMm/2r

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Total energy: E = −GMm/2r (E = U/2, K = −U/2)  ·  **Energy Relations:** For circular orbits: $K = GMm/2r$, $U = -GMm/r$, $E = -GMm/2r$. Notice $K = -U/2$ and $E = U/2$. The negative total energy confirms a bound orbit. To raise an orbit, you ADD energy (thrust), but the orbital speed *decreases* because $v_0 \propto 1/\sqrt{r}$.  ·  Higher orbit → slower speed, longer period.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: E_total = −GMm/2r: bound orbit, with K = −U/2.  ·  Astronauts float because of free fall, not absence of gravity.  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ newton: f = g m₁m₂/r²; g = gm/r²; at earth's surface g = gm/r² ≈ 9.8 m/s²..

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ 'A satellite must be above the atmosphere to feel no gravity.' ✅ A satellite feels gravity at every altitude — it is in continuous free fall. It never falls to Earth because its forward speed curves its fall into an orbit.  ·  ❌ 'Weightlessness means g = 0 on the ISS.' ✅ g at 400 km is ≈ 8.7 m/s² (89% of surface). Astronauts float because both they and the station accelerate toward Earth together (free fall).  ·  ❌ 'Heavier satellites orbit slower.' ✅ Orbital speed is independent of the satellite's mass: v₀ = √(GM/r).
